title: Amnesty urges release of protesters in ASEAN rallies in Manila
summary: Group questions police use of force as authorities defend arrests during demonstrations.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 10:42am

Protesters hold placards as they march during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on Nov. 15, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines' arm of global human rights watchdog Amnesty International has called for the immediate release of some 300 protesters arrested during demonstrations against the ASEAN summit on Sunday, November 15.
In a statement issued Sunday, the organization criticized the police response to protesters attempting to march beyond designated rally areas and barricades.
Amnesty said even demonstrations that go beyond designated protest areas remain protected by the right to peaceful assembly and should not be forcibly or violently dispersed.
"The PNP must take steps to practice restraint and strict adherence to international standards on the use of force," the organization said.
It stressed that police should use force only as a last resort, in accordance with the principles of necessity and proportionality.

Hundreds arrested in separate protests. The arrests took place as demonstrators attempted to march toward the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City, where Southeast Asian leaders are meeting for the ASEAN summit.
At Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, police blocked protesters who were trying to march toward the summit venue.
In a separate incident, more than 200 protesters were arrested in Sucat, Muntinlupa City.
Amnesty cited reports of about 300 protesters detained during the demonstrations, including nine people arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio.
Police defend arrests
The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) defended its actions, saying the arrests followed refusals to disperse and demonstrations held without permits.
In a statement, the NCRPO said maintaining public order and ensuring the safety of visiting ASEAN delegates remained its priorities.
It said the right to peaceful assembly does not permit protesters to violate the law, obstruct traffic or defy authorities.
According to the NCRPO, eight protesters were arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio and more than 200 in Sucat on November 15.
The police maintained that the arrests were made over alleged unlawful obstruction, public disruption and defiance of authorities, rather than the protesters' opinions.
The NCRPO also reported that 15 police officers were injured during confrontations at Liwasang Bonifacio.
It assured the public that those detained would receive humane treatment and due process.
However, footage shared by ABS-CBN News appeared to show police officers kicking protesters and forcing them into a crowded room in Sucat, Muntinlupa City.
Media also targeted. The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) also condemned the arrests, attempted arrests and harassment of journalists covering the demonstrations.
The group said at least 22 media workers and campus journalists reported experiencing police harassment during the protests.
Among them were two journalists arrested in Sucat, while at least three others faced attempted arrests at Liwasang Bonifacio, according to the NUJP.
